case: applies promo code discount to a return trip dispatch (line item id has #return suffix)
why: The test creates a return trip dispatch with a promo code discount and asserts the discount amount is greater than zero, which would fail if the requirement were violated.
vc: When a return trip ticket with a promo code is purchased, the Mozio email confirmation shows a promo code discount amount that is a positive number greater than zero

case: applies promo code discount to a return trip dispatch (line item id has #return suffix)
why: It sets up a return trip with a promo code discount and asserts that the resulting discount name has a length greater than zero.
vc: When a return trip ticket with a promo code is purchased, the Mozio email confirmation shows the promo code discount name as a non-empty string

case: applies promo code discount to a one-way trip dispatch (line item id has no suffix)
why: This test uses a one-way trip (no #return suffix, isReturn: false) with a promo code discount and asserts the discount amount is greater than zero, which would fail if the requirement were violated.
vc: When a one-way trip ticket with a promo code is purchased, the Mozio email confirmation continues to show the promo code discount amount as a positive number greater than zero

case: does not apply discount to a return trip dispatch when there is no promo code
why: The test creates a return trip with no discounts and asserts that report.price.discount is undefined, which would fail if a discount amount or name were present.
vc: When a return trip ticket with no promo code is purchased, the Mozio email confirmation does not display a promo code discount amount or name
